norms.quote: Outside package scripts, run it with your package manager
norms.norm: Run the void CLI through the project's package manager (npx void, pnpm void, yarn void, bunx void, vpx void) or a package script; do not rely on a global install.
norms.detect: A lint sees one JS/TS file; this concerns a command, shell, remote state or non-JS files.
norms.good: vpx void deploy or a package script

norms.quote: The CLI needs Node.js 24.22+ or 26.12+.
norms.norm: Run the void CLI on Node.js 24.22+ or 26.12+ (npx, bunx and scripts use the node on PATH; vpx uses .node-version).
norms.detect: Runtime/toolchain version, not visible in a JS file.

norms.quote: Install `void` in your project so the CLI and runtime use the same version.
norms.norm: Install the void package in the project (not only globally) so the CLI and the runtime are the same version.
norms.detect: Concerns package.json and installed versions, not a JS file.

norms.quote: Default project slug for deploy, secret, domain, and cache purge commands
norms.norm: Set VOID_PROJECT (or pass --project) to name the project for deploy, secret, domain and cache-purge commands in non-linked environments such as CI.

norms.quote: Auth token override instead of saved config
norms.norm: VOID_TOKEN overrides saved credentials; in CI supply it from a secret manager (with a matching VOID_API_URL), never commit it.

norms.quote: Inspect persistent resource names before moving their code
norms.norm: Run `void info` before moving the code of a Durable State, Room or WebSocket definition, so its persistent resource name is kept.
norms.detect: Needs the CLI's inferred name versus the lock file; multi-file.
norms.good: void info, copy name, then move

norms.quote: Loopback hosts (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `[::1]`) default to HTTP
norms.norm: For a local platform use `void connect localhost:8787` (loopback defaults to HTTP); other hostnames default to HTTPS; include a scheme to override.
norms.bad: void connect https://localhost:8787 against an HTTP-only local platform

norms.quote: saves `cloudflare.account_id` in `void.config.ts` or resolved state in `void.lock.json`
norms.norm: Treat cloudflare.account_id in void.config.ts and void.lock.json as written by `void connect`/`void init`; keep them and commit them rather than editing the account by hand.
norms.detect: Requires knowing the account state and the lock file; not a single-file shape.

norms.quote: conflicting or inaccessible account settings must be resolved before continuing
norms.norm: Resolve conflicting or inaccessible Cloudflare account settings before continuing with void connect.
norms.detect: The doc says account settings 'must be resolved before continuing'.

norms.quote: It saves credentials in your system keychain separately for each platform.
norms.norm: Void platform credentials live in the system keychain per platform origin; do not copy them into files.

norms.quote: The deployment preference is saved in `.void/project.json`.
norms.norm: The deployment destination and project link live in .void/project.json (written by void connect / void project link); change them with those commands, not by hand.

norms.quote: Use `void project link` to explicitly choose a project.
norms.norm: Choose the hosted project explicitly with `void project link`; connecting to another platform preserves the existing link.

norms.quote: In a non-interactive shell, supply a URL or explicit target.
norms.norm: In non-interactive shells pass a URL or --platform to `void connect`; Cloudflare needs usable credentials and an unambiguous account (CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID), a Void platform needs VOID_TOKEN with a matching VOID_API_URL or a valid keychain session.

norms.quote: this option is only available for Void platforms
norms.norm: Use `--no-login` only with `void connect <url>` for a Void platform; it saves the verified connection without authenticating.

norms.quote: In a non-interactive shell, pass `--platform cloudflare|void` or use
norms.norm: In a non-interactive shell pass `--platform cloudflare|void` to `void auth login/status/logout`, or use `void cloudflare` / `void account` directly.

norms.quote: for authentication does not change the project
norms.norm: Do not use `void auth login` to change the deploy target; use `void connect` for that.

norms.quote: Login fails closed when no keychain is available instead of writing the token to a plaintext file
norms.norm: `void account login` fails without a system keychain; it never writes a plaintext token file.
norms.detect: The doc says 'Login fails closed when no keychain is available'.

norms.quote: headless environments use `VOID_TOKEN` from their secret manager
norms.norm: In headless environments use VOID_TOKEN from the secret manager instead of `void account login`.

norms.quote: Connect to a platform with `void connect <url>` before logging in.
norms.norm: Run `void connect <url>` before `void account login`; if an old link has no platform URL, connect and run `void project link` again.

norms.quote: Set `VOID_API_URL` alongside `VOID_TOKEN` to identify the platform that issued it.
norms.norm: Always set VOID_API_URL together with VOID_TOKEN; both are required for environment-based auth and the URL must already be connected.

norms.quote: In a fresh CI environment, run
norms.norm: In a fresh CI environment run `void connect "$VOID_API_URL" --no-login` before deploying; to use saved login instead, unset VOID_TOKEN.

norms.quote: not combine it with a Cloudflare Access service token for CI
norms.norm: Do not use `void account token` (a human token) with a Cloudflare Access service token for CI; create a project-scoped credential with `void project token create` instead.

norms.quote: to sign in and manage credentials. No separate Cloudflare CLI is needed.
norms.norm: Sign in and manage Cloudflare credentials with `void cloudflare login/status/logout`; do not use a separate Cloudflare CLI for Void.

norms.quote: Non-interactive CI must set `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`.
norms.norm: In non-interactive CI set CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (a secret) for Cloudflare deploys.

norms.quote: Check `void cloudflare status` after switching users
norms.norm: After switching Cloudflare users run `void cloudflare status`; if the new user cannot access the pinned account_id, resolve the project target separately before deploying.

norms.quote: Explicit browser login stops with the names of these overrides
norms.norm: Remove CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN or global API key variables from the shell before an explicit browser login; environment credentials take precedence over browser credentials.
norms.detect: 'Explicit browser login stops with the names of these overrides'.

norms.quote: Before deploying, generate and review migration files with `void db generate`.
norms.norm: Use `void db push` only for prototyping; before deploying generate and review migration files with `void db generate`.

norms.quote: PostgreSQL and MySQL use `DATABASE_URL` from `.env`.
norms.norm: `void db push` and `void db reset` on PostgreSQL/MySQL act on the DATABASE_URL in .env; check it is the local database.
norms.detect: .env contents must not be read by a lint; state.

norms.quote: writes migrations under `db/migrations/`
norms.norm: Create migrations with `void db generate`; it writes them under db/migrations/ with the Drizzle snapshot and journal. Do not hand-write migration SQL for schema changes.
norms.detect: Generated non-JS files and cross-file state.

norms.quote: Review and commit the generated files before deploying.
norms.norm: Review and commit everything `void db generate` writes (SQL, snapshots, journal) before deploying.

norms.quote: It includes Void-managed auth tables and configured auth plugins, even without an application schema.
norms.norm: Expect `void db generate` to emit Void-managed auth tables and configured auth plugin tables; do not define or hand-write them in db/schema.
norms.detect: Needs the auth config and generated SQL.
norms.good: let void db generate emit it

norms.quote: If generation fails this check, the previous SQL, snapshots, and journal are restored.
norms.norm: If SQLite generation fails the fresh-database check, Void restores the previous SQL, snapshots and journal; fix the cause and rerun.
norms.detect: 'the previous SQL, snapshots, and journal are restored'.

norms.quote: rerunning generation compares snapshots and does not repair existing SQL
norms.norm: If an existing unapplied migration fails the fresh-database check, repair that migration SQL first; rerunning `void db generate` will not fix it.

norms.quote: review table rebuilds and foreign-key actions carefully
norms.norm: Review generated table rebuilds and foreign-key actions for data loss; the generation check does not verify that a migration preserves existing data.
norms.detect: Needs SQL semantics and data knowledge.

norms.quote: Direct Cloudflare PostgreSQL and MySQL projects use `DATABASE_URL` from the current shell for remote status.
norms.norm: For remote `void db status` on direct Cloudflare PostgreSQL/MySQL, export DATABASE_URL in the shell.

norms.quote: If `.env` uses the same URL as your deployment (for example after `void db connect`), reset drops the deployed tables.
norms.norm: Before `void db reset` or `void db seed`, make sure DATABASE_URL in .env is not the deployment URL (for example after `void db connect`); otherwise reset drops the deployed tables.
norms.detect: Needs the value of .env, which must not be read by a lint.

norms.quote: Pass `--yes` to skip the prompt in scripts and CI; without a terminal, the command stops unless `--yes` is set.
norms.norm: Pass --yes to `void db reset` (and seed) in scripts and CI only for a database you intend to drop; without a terminal it stops otherwise.
norms.appliesTo: void db reset, void db seed
norms.detect: 'without a terminal, the command stops unless --yes is set'.

norms.quote: Reset the local database, re-apply all migrations, then execute a seed file.
norms.norm: `void db seed` is destructive: it resets the local database before seeding; never run it against a database holding data you need.

norms.quote: If more than one default seed file exists, the CLI stops and asks you to pass `--file <path>`.
norms.norm: Keep one default seed file (db/seed.ts, .mts, .js, .mjs or .sql) or pass `--file <path>`; with several, `void db seed` stops.
norms.detect: 'the CLI stops and asks you to pass --file'.

norms.quote: If `--file` is omitted, Void looks for default seed files in this order
norms.norm: Name seed files db/seed.ts, db/seed.mts, db/seed.js, db/seed.mjs or db/seed.sql so `void db seed` finds them without --file.
norms.detect: File path check: a seed file under db/ named seed.* is one of the five default names; a differently named file (db/seeds.ts) is not found without --file. Only the path is checkable, not whether it is meant as a seed.

norms.quote: Programmatic seed modules must export either a default function or a named `seed` function.
norms.norm: A programmatic seed module (db/seed.{ts,mts,js,mjs}) must export a default function or a named `seed` function.
norms.detect: In a file whose path is db/seed.{ts,mts,js,mjs}, require an `export default <function>` or `export function seed` / `export const seed = <function>`; report files with neither.

norms.quote: Run ad-hoc SQL against the database. Provide SQL inline or from a file.
norms.norm: Use `void db execute` for ad-hoc SQL instead of hand-written scripts or other clients against the database.

norms.quote: Pass `--remote` to run against the deployed database selected in `.void/project.json`
norms.norm: `void db execute --remote` runs against the deployed database; use it deliberately and check the target in .void/project.json first.

norms.quote: uses `DATABASE_URL` from the current shell; Cloudflare cannot return the password from Hyperdrive.
norms.norm: For --remote on direct Cloudflare PostgreSQL/MySQL, set DATABASE_URL in the current shell (Cloudflare cannot return the Hyperdrive password).

norms.quote: a `--file` larger than 100 KB runs as a D1 import
norms.norm: Do not run a --file larger than 100 KB with `void db execute --remote` against a live direct Cloudflare D1 database unless you accept that it cannot serve queries until the import finishes and no rows are printed.
norms.good: split the file or accept downtime

norms.quote: you will be prompted to confirm before the query is sent to the deployed database
norms.norm: Destructive SQL (DELETE, UPDATE, DROP) with --remote prompts in a TTY; pass --yes only when intended; non-TTY (CI) never prompts.

norms.quote: Apply pending migrations to the local database without resetting.
norms.norm: Use `void db migrate` (not reset) to apply pending migrations while preserving local data.
norms.bad: void db reset to apply one migration

norms.quote: Pass `--remote` to apply pending migrations to the saved target.
norms.norm: `void db migrate --remote` applies migrations to the deployed target; hosted projects need a Void login and link; direct PostgreSQL/MySQL use the shell DATABASE_URL.

norms.quote: The D1 binding must set `migrations_dir`.
norms.norm: Set migrations_dir on the D1 binding so `void db migrate --remote` can use the binding's migration directory.
norms.detect: In void.config.ts, a D1 binding object literal passed to the Cloudflare/database config has no `migrations_dir` property. Escapes: bindings built from variables or spreads, and bindings kept in void.lock.json.
norms.bad:
// void.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ cloudflare: { d1_databases: [{ binding: 'DB' }] } });
norms.good:
// void.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ cloudflare: { d1_databases: [{ binding: 'DB', migrations_dir: 'db/migrations' }] } });

norms.quote: If the URL isn't stored yet, run `void db set-url` first.
norms.norm: Before `void db studio --remote` on a hosted PostgreSQL/MySQL project, run `void db set-url` if the URL is not stored.

norms.quote: **D1 projects**: use `void db execute --remote` to query the deployed database.
norms.norm: For a deployed D1 database use `void db execute --remote`; `void db studio --remote` does not apply.

norms.quote: Use the bookmark printed before deployment migrations, or an ISO 8601 timestamp with a timezone
norms.norm: To restore a direct Cloudflare D1 database use `void db restore` with the bookmark printed before deployment migrations, or an ISO 8601 timestamp with timezone.

norms.quote: Reverse older migrations with a new migration.
norms.norm: Time Travel keeps 7 days (Workers Free) or 30 days (Workers Paid); for older changes write a new reversing migration.

norms.quote: Restoring discards every write made after the selected point.
norms.norm: `void db restore` is destructive: it discards every write after the restore point; `--yes` skips confirmation in scripts and CI.

norms.quote: Roll back the code with [`void project rollback`](./project.md#void-project-rollback-deployid) if the live version needs the newer schema.
norms.norm: To recover from a bad migration: (1) roll back code with `void project rollback` if the live version needs the newer schema, (2) restore the database with the printed bookmark, (3) fix or remove the failed migration before deploying again (the restore rewinds migration history).

norms.quote: For a one-off Cloudflare deployment, add `--platform cloudflare` to restore, rollback, and deploy commands.
norms.norm: For a one-off Cloudflare deployment pass --platform cloudflare to restore, rollback and deploy alike.
norms.appliesTo: void db restore / project rollback / deploy

norms.quote: rename migrations from numeric prefixes (`0001_name.sql`) to timestamps
norms.norm: `void db rename-migrations` is for linked Void platform projects only (sign in and `void project link` first); on direct Cloudflare keep existing filenames; new migrations use timestamps.

norms.quote: The command saves `DATABASE_URL` in `.env`.
norms.norm: `void db connect` writes DATABASE_URL to .env; keep .env uncommitted. With a linked Void project it also updates the encrypted deployment URL unless --local-only.

norms.quote: configure the same URL as a protected `DATABASE_URL` in the shell or CI environment that runs deploy.
norms.norm: For direct Cloudflare deploys set DATABASE_URL as a protected (secret) variable in the shell or CI environment that runs deploy.

norms.quote: adopt its applied migration history](../../guide/database.md#adopt-existing-drizzle) before the first Void deployment
norms.norm: For an existing PostgreSQL database migrated by Drizzle, adopt its applied migration history before the first Void deployment.

norms.quote: Update the PostgreSQL or MySQL connection string for deployment.
norms.norm: `void db set-url` is only for projects with database pg or mysql; it sends the connection string to the platform API to create or update Hyperdrive.

norms.quote: use `pg_dump` for a complete backup
norms.norm: For PostgreSQL schemas with views, triggers, custom types, functions or standalone sequences use pg_dump for a complete backup; `void db export` only dumps the local database.

norms.quote: Dump the local database as SQL.
norms.norm: `void db export` dumps the local database only (stdout or --output); use it for local dumps, not as a production backup.

norms.quote: Deploying to a Void platform requires an explicit connection with `void connect <url>`.
norms.norm: Run `void connect <url>` before deploying to a Void platform; a saved project URL or VOID_API_URL alone does not connect.

norms.quote: In fresh CI environments, run `void connect "$VOID_API_URL" --no-login` first.
norms.norm: In fresh CI run `void connect "$VOID_API_URL" --no-login` before `void deploy`.

norms.quote: Pressing Ctrl+C stops observation; use `void project cancel` to request cancellation
norms.norm: Ctrl+C on `void deploy` only stops watching; cancel with `void project cancel`, inspect with `void project status`, and wait for an interrupted recovery's result before deploying again.
norms.appliesTo: void deploy on a Void platform
norms.good: void project status, wait, then deploy

norms.quote: check `void project status` before trying another deployment.
norms.norm: If `void deploy` times out (waits up to 30 minutes), check `void project status` before another deployment.

norms.quote: Keep the first deployment focused on the existing app.
norms.norm: When adopting an existing Void Worker, keep the first deployment focused on the existing app (deploy links the Worker and migrates its root Cloudflare config).

norms.quote: deploy stops and tells you to run `void db generate`, review the migration, commit it yourself, and rerun `void deploy`.
norms.norm: If deploy's read-only schema drift check finds a new migration would be generated, run `void db generate`, review, commit it yourself, then rerun `void deploy`.
norms.detect: 'deploy stops and tells you to run void db generate'.

norms.quote: Target a specific Void project by slug; not supported with `--platform cloudflare`
norms.norm: Do not pass --project with --platform cloudflare; the Worker and account come from void.config.ts and void.lock.json.

norms.quote: Skip the build step; on Cloudflare this is supported for static/SPA/SSG deploys only
norms.norm: Use --skip-build on Cloudflare only for static/SPA/SSG output; Worker apps cannot skip the build.

norms.quote: Deploy without applying application or authentication SQL migrations; supported on Cloudflare and Void platforms
norms.norm: --skip-migrations deploys without application or authentication SQL; use it only when migrations run separately or the database is shared with a preview.

norms.quote: Fail when email cannot be set up instead of deploying without it
norms.norm: Pass --require-email (with --platform cloudflare) in CI so a deploy fails instead of shipping without email.

norms.quote: Run resource provisioning again even when every resource exists; requires `--platform cloudflare`
norms.norm: --provision re-runs resource provisioning even when all resources exist; use only on Cloudflare and only when intended.

norms.quote: Publish an existing Durable Object Worker directly; readiness is checked after traffic changes
norms.norm: --atomic publishes an existing Durable Object Worker directly (readiness is checked after traffic changes); apply it to one deployment only when staged deploys cannot stage.

norms.quote: set `deploy: { cloudflare: { mode: 'atomic' } }` in `void.config.ts`
norms.norm: For a Durable Object Worker that consistently cannot stage, set deploy.cloudflare.mode to 'atomic' in void.config.ts; the default is 'staged'.
norms.detect: Whether it is needed needs deploy history.

norms.quote: The code must work with the database's current schema.
norms.norm: With --skip-migrations the code must work with the database's current schema; the next deploy without the flag applies pending migrations.

norms.quote: Keep migration files and schema validation in place.
norms.norm: When using --skip-migrations keep migration files and schema validation in place; Durable Object class migrations still run when publishing code. If the Void platform does not support the flag, upgrade it first.

norms.quote: Use `--debug` or `VOID_DEPLOY_DEBUG=1` to mirror it to stderr.
norms.norm: Every deploy writes a JSONL log to ~/.void/logs/; use --debug or VOID_DEPLOY_DEBUG=1 to mirror it to stderr when diagnosing a failure.

norms.quote: Keep credentials out of build commands and register them as CI secrets
norms.norm: Keep credentials out of build commands; register them as CI secrets so the CI provider can mask them in logs.
norms.detect: In a JS/TS file under scripts or config, a string literal passed to a build command or exec call looks like a credential (KEY=, token pattern). Only inline literals are caught; secrets in YAML/CI files and env interpolation escape.
norms.good:
// scripts/build.ts
execSync('vp build'); // API_KEY comes from the CI secret

norms.quote: Selecting Skip deployment setup stores `"platform": "none"`; a later `void deploy` stops
norms.norm: With platform none in .void/project.json `void deploy` stops until a platform override (--platform) is given.
norms.detect: 'a later void deploy stops with guidance'.

norms.quote: In CI (non-TTY), `void deploy` errors out instead
norms.norm: In CI with no linked project set VOID_PROJECT or pass --project <slug> to `void deploy`.
norms.detect: 'In CI (non-TTY), void deploy errors out instead'.

norms.quote: `VOID_API_URL` selects the platform and `--project` selects its project.
norms.norm: To deploy once to another connected Void platform: `void connect <url>`, then `VOID_API_URL=<url> void deploy --platform void --project <slug>`; you must name the project when overriding a different platform's saved link.

norms.quote: In CI, set `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and, if the token can access several accounts, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
norms.norm: For `void deploy --platform cloudflare` in CI set CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and, for multi-account tokens, CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID.

norms.quote: Unavailable; use the top-level `cloudflare` config
norms.norm: Do not use named (wrangler-style) environments with a direct Cloudflare deploy; use the top-level cloudflare config in void.config.ts.
norms.detect: In void.config.ts, a `cloudflare` object contains an `env`/`environments` property. Escapes: config assembled from variables.
norms.bad:
// void.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ cloudflare: { env: { staging: {} } } });
norms.good:
// void.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ cloudflare: { name: 'app' } });

norms.quote: Needed in fresh CI when a workers.dev Worker has no preview URL
norms.norm: In fresh CI set CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_SUBDOMAIN when a workers.dev Worker has no preview URL (not needed when workers_dev is false).

norms.quote: Lets Access credentials reach the readiness check on a route or Custom Domain
norms.norm: Set CF_ACCESS_READINESS_ORIGIN (for example https://app.example.com) so Access credentials reach the readiness check on a route or Custom Domain.

norms.quote: Required in the deploy environment for PostgreSQL or MySQL provisioning and migrations
norms.norm: Provide DATABASE_URL in the deploy environment for PostgreSQL or MySQL provisioning and migrations on Cloudflare.

norms.quote: direct Cloudflare deployment history shows the applied migration state as unknown
norms.norm: After --skip-migrations the deployment history shows migration state as unknown, and rolling back code does not reverse database changes.

norms.quote: Commit `void.lock.json` after the first deploy before using other machines or CI.
norms.norm: Commit void.lock.json after the first direct Cloudflare deploy, before using other machines or CI.
norms.detect: Git state of a non-JS file.

norms.quote: The token needs Workers Scripts: Edit, read access to bound resources, and edit access to products Void provisions.
norms.norm: Give the Cloudflare API token Workers Scripts: Edit, read access to bound resources and edit access to products Void provisions.

norms.quote: Use `void secret put <NAME>` for production server values. Local `.env` values are never deployed.
norms.norm: Set production server values with `void secret put <NAME>`; local .env values are never deployed.

norms.quote: Run `void db generate` and commit schema changes before deploying.
norms.norm: Run `void db generate` and commit schema changes before deploying.

norms.quote: Sandbox requires [Workers Paid]
norms.norm: Sandbox needs Workers Paid, Docker and Containers access; API tokens need Account / Containers: Edit and Account / Cloudchamber: Edit.

norms.quote: set `email.from` and run `void email setup --platform cloudflare` locally
norms.norm: For email on direct Cloudflare set email.from, run `void email setup --platform cloudflare` locally, commit the lock file and pass --require-email in CI.

norms.quote: Convert a legacy singular `route` field to a `routes` array first so adding the domain cannot shadow the existing route.
norms.norm: Before `void domain add` on a direct Cloudflare project, convert a legacy singular `route` field to a `routes` array so the new custom domain cannot shadow it.
norms.detect: In void.config.ts, the cloudflare config object has a `route` property (singular) instead of `routes`. Escapes: config built via variables or spreads.
norms.bad:
// void.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ cloudflare: { route: 'example.com/*' } });
norms.good:
// void.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ cloudflare: { routes: ['example.com/*'] } });

norms.quote: Wildcard custom hostnames (`*.example.com`) are not supported
norms.norm: Register each subdomain individually; wildcard custom hostnames (*.example.com) are not supported.
norms.detect: Command argument (also a string in void.config.ts routes, not a JS-detectable intent).

norms.quote: Direct Cloudflare projects add a `custom_domain` route and immediately synchronize only the route configuration
norms.norm: `void domain add` on a direct Cloudflare project edits the custom_domain route in config and applies it immediately (cron, queue and workflow triggers unchanged); the zone must be on the pinned account.

norms.quote: Deleting the final custom domain uses your browser session from `void cloudflare login` or an API token with Workers Scripts: Edit permission.
norms.norm: `void domain delete` on direct Cloudflare applies immediately; deleting the last domain needs void cloudflare login or an API token with Workers Scripts: Edit.

norms.quote: For direct Cloudflare projects, status reports whether the route is present in the Void Cloudflare config.
norms.norm: `void domain status` for direct Cloudflare reports only whether the route is in config (not certificate state); --project is for hosted projects only.

norms.quote: `void email setup` and `void email status --platform cloudflare` are the exception
norms.norm: `void email setup` and `void email status --platform cloudflare` act on your own Cloudflare account via `void cloudflare login` and need no Void project; other email commands resolve project by --project, VOID_PROJECT, linked project.

norms.quote: Reserved submissions count toward the limit; started attempts remain charged even if delivery fails or its outcome is unknown.
norms.norm: Reserved and started email attempts count toward the monthly limit even if delivery fails; check `void email usage` before bulk sends.

norms.quote: Provider acceptance does not confirm mailbox delivery; inspect unknown outcomes before retrying.
norms.norm: Inspect unknown email outcomes with `void email logs` before retrying a send; provider acceptance is not mailbox delivery.

norms.quote: Outbound mail is only delivered to verified addresses.
norms.norm: Outbound mail on the Void platform reaches only verified destinations; check `void email destinations`.

norms.quote: until it has, a send to that address returns `UNVERIFIED_DESTINATION` for that recipient
norms.norm: After `void email allow <address>`, the recipient must click the verification link and you must run `void email destinations` to record it; until then sends return UNVERIFIED_DESTINATION.

norms.quote: If the link did not arrive or has expired, run `void email allow <address>` again while the address is still pending
norms.norm: If the verification link did not arrive or expired, rerun `void email allow <address>` while the address is still pending.

norms.quote: so it skips this step but not the verification
norms.norm: The project owner's email is added automatically but still needs verification: click the mailed link and run `void email destinations`.

norms.quote: New sends to that address are refused immediately; previously admitted attempts may finish. No deploy is involved.
norms.norm: `void email disallow` takes effect immediately without a deploy.

norms.quote: An alias is permanent and reserved until the project is deleted.
norms.norm: `void email alias <name>` is permanent and reserved until the project is deleted; choose carefully, names of five characters or fewer need a plan allowing short names; use --yes in scripts.

norms.quote: redeploy with the current Void version so handlers receive the expected `message.to` address
norms.norm: Before sharing an email alias, redeploy with the current Void version so handlers receive the expected message.to; check readiness with `void email alias`.

norms.quote: Send and receive at your own domain on a Cloudflare zone you own, registered to the project.
norms.norm: `void email domain` is Void-platform only; on your own Cloudflare account the mail domain comes from email.from.

norms.quote: Custom inbound email requires a Cloudflare zone apex because its catch-all does not cover subdomains.
norms.norm: Register a Cloudflare zone apex for custom inbound email; if the apex already receives mail use another apex or the shared address (foreign MX records and catch-alls are preserved). Each apex belongs to one project.

norms.quote: Use `sync` to reconcile setup and refresh readiness.
norms.norm: Use `void email domain sync <domain>` to reconcile setup and refresh readiness; a blocked or uncertain operation exits unsuccessfully and names the operation to inspect.

norms.quote: Inbound delivery must be ready; run `void email domain sync <domain>` first if setup is incomplete.
norms.norm: Before `void email domain rotate-secret` ensure inbound delivery is ready (run sync first); the secret is shared with other domains on the zone; inspect an uncertain result before retrying.

norms.quote: Disable the domain assignment and record cleanup.
norms.norm: `void email domain remove` disables the assignment and cleans up records; zone resources used by another domain remain; unfinished cleanup stays recorded.

norms.quote: `void email status` reads only your own Cloudflare account, so `--platform cloudflare` is required.
norms.norm: Pass --platform cloudflare to `void email status`; on the Void platform use `void email usage` and `void email destinations`.

norms.quote: Exits unsuccessfully when setup is incomplete or cannot be verified.
norms.norm: `void email status --platform cloudflare` exits non-zero when setup is incomplete; use it as a CI/pre-deploy check.
norms.detect: 'Exits unsuccessfully when setup is incomplete or cannot be verified.'

norms.quote: Requires `email.from` in `void.config.ts`, an interactive terminal, and Cloudflare email permissions.
norms.norm: `void email setup --platform cloudflare` requires email.from in void.config.ts, an interactive terminal and Cloudflare email permissions; run it locally, not in CI.

norms.quote: Commit `void.lock.json`, then run `void deploy --platform cloudflare --require-email` in CI.
norms.norm: After `void email setup`, commit void.lock.json, then deploy in CI with `void deploy --platform cloudflare --require-email`.

norms.quote: Run this command again after upgrading to Workers Paid to enable arbitrary recipients.
norms.norm: On Workers Free, sending-only apps need Email Sending (Workers Paid); rerun `void email setup --platform cloudflare` after upgrading.

norms.quote: Scaffold a Drizzle table, list and create routes, and a route to fetch one row by ID.
norms.norm: Scaffold a table with its routes using `void gen model <name> [name:type...]` instead of writing them by hand.
norms.detect: Use the command, not hand-writing; a lint cannot know a file should have been generated.

norms.quote: `db/schema/posts.ts`: a table with `id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, and your columns
norms.norm: `void gen model` writes db/schema/<name>.ts (table with id, createdAt, updatedAt and the given columns), an export from db/schema.ts, routes/api/<name>/index.ts (GET list, POST insert with validation), routes/api/<name>/[id].ts (GET by id with 404), and regenerates .void/ types; edit the generated files rather than rerunning (existing files are never overwritten).
norms.detect: Cross-file shape; each table must also be exported from db/schema.ts.

norms.quote: Run `void db push` to apply the schema locally, or `void db generate` to create migrations before deploying.
norms.norm: After `void gen model`, apply the schema locally with `void db push`, or create migrations with `void db generate` before deploying.

norms.quote: The generated routes automatically detect your validation library from `package.json`
norms.norm: `void gen model` detects valibot, zod or arktype from package.json; with none it asks you to choose or skip validation.

norms.quote: Column format: `name:type` or `name:type?` (nullable).
norms.norm: Give `void gen model` columns as name:type or name:type? (nullable) with types string, text, datetime, integer, boolean, real, blob.

norms.quote: Model names must be lowercase alphanumeric with underscores
norms.norm: Model names must be lowercase alphanumeric with underscores (posts, user_roles); existing files are never overwritten.

norms.quote: Create an empty migration file with a timestamp prefix (`YYYYMMDDHHMMSS`).
norms.norm: Create an empty custom migration with `void gen migration <name>` (writes db/migrations/<YYYYMMDDHHMMSS>_<name>.sql); do not number migration files by hand.
norms.detect: Non-JS file name; lint sees JS only.

norms.quote: Existing projects using the old numeric prefix (`0001_`, `0002_`, ...) can rename with `void db rename-migrations`.
norms.norm: Migrate old numeric-prefix migration files with `void db rename-migrations`, not by hand.

norms.quote: Create a route file with `defineHandler` exports. Defaults to GET.
norms.norm: Create route files with `void gen route <path> [--methods get,post,...]` (supported: get, post, put, patch, delete); the file routes/<path>.ts exports one defineHandler per method.
norms.detect: In a file under routes/ (not starting with _), each exported HTTP-method binding (get, post, put, patch, delete) must be initialised with a defineHandler(...) call. Escapes: handlers wrapped in helper factories or re-exported from another module.
norms.bad:
// routes/api/health.ts
export const get = (c) => c.json({ ok: true });
norms.good:
// routes/api/health.ts
export const get = defineHandler((c) => c.json({ ok: true }));

norms.quote: Create a numbered middleware file with `defineMiddleware` default export.
norms.norm: Create middleware with `void gen middleware <name>`; the file is middleware/NN.<name>.ts (numeric prefix auto-detected) with a defineMiddleware default export.
norms.detect: In a file under middleware/, the default export must be a defineMiddleware(...) call; also the file name must start with a numeric prefix (NN.).
norms.good:
// middleware/01.auth.ts
export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => next());

norms.quote: Scaffold SSR entry points and a minimal App component for your framework.
norms.norm: Scaffold SSR entries with `void gen ssr [--react|--vue|--svelte|--solid]` (auto-detected from package.json if omitted): src/main.ssr.{tsx,ts} server entry with defineRender, src/main.client.{tsx,ts} client entry with hydration, src/App.{tsx,vue,svelte}.
norms.detect: In src/main.ssr.{ts,tsx}, require a defineRender(...) call (default export or exported); absent defineRender is reported. Escapes: renderer defined in another module and re-exported.

norms.quote: Create a cron job file in `crons/` with `defineScheduled` and a placeholder cron expression.
norms.norm: Create cron jobs with `void gen cron <name>`; files live in crons/ and use defineScheduled with a cron expression.
norms.detect: In a file under crons/, the default export must be a defineScheduled(...) call (with a cron expression string).

norms.quote: Create a queue consumer file in `queues/` with `defineQueue`, a `Message` type, and commented-out batch options.
norms.norm: Create queue consumers with `void gen queue <name>`; files live in queues/ and use defineQueue.
norms.detect: In a file under queues/, the default export must be a defineQueue(...) call.

norms.quote: A GitHub identity can belong to only one Void account.
norms.norm: A GitHub identity links to only one Void account; if already linked elsewhere, sign in to that account or authorize a different GitHub identity.

norms.quote: After installing, run `void github connect` to link a repository to your project.
norms.norm: After `void github install`, run `void github connect` to link the repository to the project.

norms.quote: Each entry includes the `[id: <installation_id>]` needed for `--installation` in non-interactive use.
norms.norm: Use `void github installations` to find the installation ID for --installation in non-interactive use.

norms.quote: Run `join` locally before non-interactive setup when needed.
norms.norm: Run `void github join` locally (browser) before non-interactive setup of an organization installation.

norms.quote: On every push to the configured branch, Void builds and deploys your project automatically.
norms.norm: `void github connect` makes every push to the configured branch deploy automatically; choose the branch deliberately.

norms.quote: **required in non-interactive mode**
norms.norm: In non-interactive mode pass --branch (and --installation / --repo when they cannot be selected automatically) to `void github connect`.

norms.quote: Choose `container` for platform builds or `github_actions` for a deployment workflow.
norms.norm: Choose --executor container (platform builds, default) or github_actions (deployment workflow); pass flags to skip prompts.

norms.quote: The workflow must be a `.yml` or `.yaml` file under `.github/workflows/`.
norms.norm: With github_actions the --workflow file must be a .yml/.yaml under .github/workflows/ (default void-deploy.yml); only that workflow can obtain the project's OIDC deployment token.

norms.quote: Prefer a dedicated deployment workflow.
norms.norm: Use a dedicated deployment workflow file for the OIDC deploy token, not a general-purpose workflow.

norms.quote: Organization connections require repository authorization in a local browser first.
norms.norm: For organization connections authorize the repository in a local browser before CI setup.

norms.quote: Running `void github connect` on a project that is already connected fails.
norms.norm: A project has one GitHub connection; run `void github disconnect` before connecting a different repository.
norms.detect: 'on a project that is already connected fails'.

norms.quote: To change the repository, disconnect and reconnect.
norms.norm: `void github update` changes only branch, executor or workflow; to change the repository disconnect and reconnect. In CI pass at least one of --branch, --executor, --workflow.

norms.quote: Any in-flight builds for the project are cancelled before the connection is removed.
norms.norm: `void github disconnect` stops automatic deploys and cancels in-flight builds; --yes is required in non-interactive shells.

norms.quote: `--yes` is **required** in a non-interactive shell (CI)
norms.norm: Pass --yes to `void github disconnect` in non-interactive shells.
norms.detect: '--yes is required in a non-interactive shell'.

norms.quote: Builds run on **GitHub Actions** keep their logs on GitHub
norms.norm: `void build logs` streams only container builds; GitHub Actions builds keep logs on GitHub (the command prints the run URL); only the last 10,000 lines of a container build are retained.

norms.quote: If the platform cannot confirm it, upgrade the platform runtime or read the retained logs without `--follow`.
norms.norm: If `void build logs --follow` cannot confirm the final tail, upgrade the platform runtime or read retained logs without --follow; an unfinished tail errors after two minutes; retry.

norms.quote: Use `--plan` to preview changes and affected accounts, then `--yes` to apply them in a script.
norms.norm: Preview with --plan, then apply with --yes in scripts for `void platform config plans` changes; lower quotas can restrict accounts already above them.

norms.quote: Choose another signup default before archiving the current one.
norms.norm: Choose another signup default plan before archiving the current one; `remove` needs --replacement when the plan has accounts or is the signup default.

norms.quote: Build timeouts have a platform maximum of 60 minutes; `0` uses that maximum.
norms.norm: In plan files limits are nonnegative whole numbers; 0 means unlimited by the plan; build timeouts max 60 minutes; buildInstanceType is standard-3 or standard-4; aiLogging off|metadata|full|inherit; storage quotas are not editable.

norms.quote: If someone changes the plans after your preview, create a new preview before applying.
norms.norm: If plans change after your preview, create a new preview before applying.

norms.quote: Run `void platform config plans sync --yes` to continue before editing plans again.
norms.norm: If plan updates fail or stall, run `void platform config plans sync --yes` before editing plans again; after a lost connection inspect `show` and operator events before retrying.
norms.detect: 'the command exits with a nonzero status and the configuration stays saved'.

norms.quote: When configuring an existing installation for the first time, run
norms.norm: On an existing installation run `void platform config auth initialize` once, then sign in again.

norms.quote: account is a separate, explicit action. Before disabling a method, verify a linked
norms.norm: Before disabling a login method verify a linked alternative; the last method cannot be disabled, and disabling signs out its users including administrators (a login token used as VOID_TOKEN is revoked; scoped deployment tokens stay valid).

norms.quote: For scripted configuration, use `--file <path>` for the
norms.norm: In scripts pass nonsecret fields with --file and secrets by environment variable name with --client-secret-env; for enable/link supply --test-id from a completed test.

norms.quote: Protection changes require installation ownership, the saved recovery credentials,
norms.norm: `void platform config auth protection enable/disable` needs installation ownership, saved recovery credentials and a signed-in administrator, and signs out all users; change dependent signup rules before removing protection.

norms.quote: Recovery requires Cloudflare management/database authority,
norms.norm: `void platform config auth recover` needs Cloudflare management/database authority, original recovery keys and a successful browser provider test; with --yes the file needs exact expectedIdentity issuer and subject.

norms.quote: `attempt-resolve` records `outcome_unknown`, retains its quota charge
norms.norm: Use `attempt-resolve` only after the original Worker execution has ended and the attempt is at least 24 hours old; --ended is your attestation; keep recipient addresses and message content out of --reason; the send is never retried.

norms.quote: `operation-resolve` recovers a Cloudflare routing, Worker, secret, catch-all, or
norms.norm: Use `operation-resolve` only after the operation is at least 24 hours old; inspect the exact resource in the preview and attest applied or not-applied; restore the matching platform version first; time alone never retries.

norms.quote: A missing rule alone is insufficient evidence for `not-applied`.
norms.norm: For `shared-recipient-resolve` inspect the exact account/zone/recipient/rule named by --plan and use Cloudflare's provider audit; a missing rule alone is not evidence of not-applied.

norms.quote: `domain-add` uses the platform's Cloudflare credential for zones in its account.
norms.norm: For a zone in another account pipe a scoped Cloudflare API token on standard input with --token-stdin --yes; use --outbound-only if the apex MX records belong to another provider; managed inbound needs the zone apex.

norms.quote: If project deletion leaves cleanup blocked by an expired or revoked Cloudflare token
norms.norm: Use `domain-remove <domain> --token-stdin --yes` with a replacement token for the same account and zone only for blocked cleanup after project deletion; for a live project renew the token via domain-add.

norms.quote: `policy` decides which recipients a project's
norms.norm: `policy-set <verified|domains|any>` widens which recipients the shared sender reaches (default verified); platform-domain addresses stay verified-only; Cloudflare still refuses unverified destinations until the platform mail domain is onboarded for Sending.

norms.quote: Installation name used in `void-<name>-<role>` resource names; choose an unused name
norms.norm: Choose an unused installation --name (resources are void-<name>-<role>).

norms.quote: External PostgreSQL and a configured login method are required in either mode.
norms.norm: A platform install needs external PostgreSQL and at least one login method; non-interactive install defaults to GitHub when none is supplied; --workers-dev cannot be combined with --application-domain, --zone or --dedicated-zone.

norms.quote: Installation that writes DNS or creates a zone needs a management API token.
norms.norm: Scripts supply CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN or CF_API_TOKEN (a management token) for installs that write DNS or create a zone; the runtime token is separate.

norms.quote: supplying only one is an error
norms.norm: Set both VOID_EMAIL_SENDER_DOMAIN and VOID_EMAIL_SHARED_ZONE_ID to enable platform email during install or upgrade; one alone is an error.

norms.quote: The URL must be an HTTPS origin without credentials, a
norms.norm: --dashboard-url must be an HTTPS origin without credentials, path, query or fragment.

norms.quote: Use an empty PostgreSQL database dedicated to the installation.
norms.norm: Use an empty PostgreSQL database dedicated to the installation; after it is claimed or Hyperdrive provisioned, a different URL is rejected.

norms.quote: An existing Hyperdrive must point to the platform database with SQL result caching disabled.
norms.norm: An existing Hyperdrive must point at the platform database with SQL result caching disabled; supply a database owner URL for migrations.

norms.quote: Without one, supply a base64-encoded 32-byte `VOID_PLATFORM_RECOVERY_KEY`.
norms.norm: Recovery secrets use the system keychain; without one supply a base64 32-byte VOID_PLATFORM_RECOVERY_KEY and keep original credentials in protected CI secrets.

norms.quote: Installation progress and partial credentials are saved encrypted locally.
norms.norm: Resume unfinished setup by rerunning the installer or `void platform install --resume --name <id>`; use lifecycle commands for completed installations.

norms.quote: Commands that make changes also require `--yes`; `--plan` only previews changes.
norms.norm: Lifecycle commands (upgrade, rollback, repair, disable, enable, uninstall) need a slug or ID when several installations exist, and --yes to apply; preview with --plan.

norms.quote: Lifecycle commands require local installation records; use `discover` to restore them on another machine.
norms.norm: Lifecycle commands require local installation records; run `void platform discover` on another machine and set VOID_PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL.

norms.quote: Preview with `--plan` first. Existing Access protection must cover the configured
norms.norm: Preview dashboard-url changes with --plan first; existing Access protection must cover the dashboard origin.

norms.quote: Platform migrations only move forward.
norms.norm: Platform migrations only move forward; `rollback` restores an earlier runtime without reversing PostgreSQL migrations and refuses incompatible targets (pass --runtime and, for custom builds, --from-runtime).

norms.quote: Data resources are retained unless you pass `--purge-data`.
norms.norm: `void platform uninstall` retains data unless --purge-data; --purge-resources includes --purge-data and deletes Workers, Queues, R2, AI Gateway, DNS record, routes, custom domains and installer-created Access resources; read the policy first. --keep-zone is deprecated.

norms.quote: It refuses before any change while projects remain or resource reads are denied.
norms.norm: `--purge-resources` refuses while projects remain or reads are denied; use the Edit permissions listed by --plan; rerun the same command to continue after an interruption.
norms.detect: 'It refuses before any change while projects remain'.

norms.quote: Add an application domain to a workers.dev test platform.
norms.norm: `void platform domain set` adds an application domain to a workers.dev test platform; replacing a configured application domain is unsupported; rerun the same command to resume; --plan is read-only; --yes required non-interactively.

norms.quote: `--plan` validates the change and prints its effect without applying it.
norms.norm: Preview operator changes with --plan and apply with --yes (required in scripts); do not combine them; they do not apply to authentication commands.

norms.quote: Void does not automatically retry changes.
norms.norm: If an operator change times out or loses connection, inspect affected objects and `void platform system events` before repeating it; partial results exit nonzero.

norms.quote: For automation, supply `VOID_OPERATOR_TOKEN` with an explicit `VOID_API_URL` or `--connection`.
norms.norm: For automation supply VOID_OPERATOR_TOKEN with an explicit VOID_API_URL or --connection; keep it separate from deployment credentials.

norms.quote: Without `--connection`, Void uses `VOID_API_URL` if set, then the active platform connection.
norms.norm: Select the platform with --connection <slug-or-url>; otherwise VOID_API_URL then the active connection is used; project files do not change this.

norms.quote: `use` and `status` accept an installation slug, display name, saved ID, or API URL.
norms.norm: If a slug or name matches several platforms use the API URL with `void platform use/status`; non-interactive use needs an explicit selector.

norms.quote: A deployment that has begun switching traffic, is compensating for a failure, or has finished cannot be canceled through this command.
norms.norm: Cancel a deployment only while pending, uploading, migrating or prerendering (or canceling).

norms.quote: `migrate-assets` copies a deployment's legacy assets to scoped R2 storage
norms.norm: Preview `deployment migrate-assets` with --plan and resume with --cursor; original assets remain.

norms.quote: Following stops with an error if a window exceeds 10,000 records
norms.norm: With `deployment logs --follow` use a narrower historical query if a window exceeds 10,000 records; --limit 1-500; --since accepts 10m, 2h, 1d, ISO date or epoch ms.
norms.detect: 'Following stops with an error if a window exceeds 10,000 records'.

norms.quote: Container log retrieval requires managed builds to be enabled.
norms.norm: `platform build logs` needs managed builds enabled for containers; GitHub Actions builds return an external log URL; follow errors if completion is not confirmed within two minutes.

norms.quote: `rotate-proxy-tokens` gives projects new platform credentials on their live Worker
norms.norm: `rotate-proxy-tokens` rotates platform credentials without redeploy: use --plan then --yes; a rotation takes about 6 minutes per project; repeating --yes while running starts another rotation; WebSocket connections reconnect once; old credentials stop working when finished.

norms.quote: `sandbox-drain` removes legacy tenant-owned Sandbox resources.
norms.norm: `sandbox-drain` is destructive and pauses application traffic during cleanup; --plan then --yes, continue with --cursor.

norms.quote: They are unavailable on a self-hosted installation
norms.norm: `void platform worker` commands manage hosted Void Cloud Workers only; on self-hosted use the lifecycle commands; preview rollbacks with --plan.

norms.quote: Deleting a user also deletes their project resources.
norms.norm: `void platform user delete` deletes the user's project resources; the last active administrator cannot be deleted or suspended; preview with --plan.

norms.quote: Suspending a user blocks their apps, scheduled jobs, and queue consumers.
norms.norm: Suspending a user blocks apps, cron and queue consumers, and queue messages are dropped when retries run out (about 3 hours with default retries); restore a mistaken suspension promptly.

norms.quote: `delete` removes the project and its resources.
norms.norm: `void platform project delete` removes the project and its resources; `owner` transfers the project (preview with --plan; former owner becomes administrator; CI deploy credentials are revoked).

norms.quote: If deployment reports that a project requires normalization, an operator can preview
norms.norm: When deploy reports a project requires normalization, run `void platform project normalize <id> --plan` then --yes; it refuses while deployment or recovery is active.

norms.quote: Only platform administrators can change the setting. Apps cannot override it.
norms.norm: AI logging is set per project by administrators with `void platform project ai-logging <project-id> <inherit|off|metadata|full>`; apps cannot override it; new installations enable gateway logging, so prompts and responses are stored unless disabled.

norms.quote: Project settings require platform 1.8.0 or later.
norms.norm: AI logging project settings need platform 1.8.0+; run `void platform upgrade` otherwise.

norms.quote: Quote wildcard patterns in your shell.
norms.norm: Quote wildcard patterns such as '*@example.com' in `void platform signup allow/disallow`; identity grants match connection ID and subject exactly.

norms.quote: Send accepts up to 100 comma-separated addresses.
norms.norm: `invitation send` accepts up to 100 addresses; invitations grant signup access even if email fails; share /invite or `void connect '<platform URL>'` yourself when no email is sent.

norms.quote: The platform also repairs unpublished settings every hour.
norms.norm: For failed AI logging changes see the error table: ai_logging_publish_failed (not saved, retry), ai_logging_publish_pending (retry to publish), ai_logging_policy_unavailable/invalid (HTTP 503; retry or set the mode again); check state with `void platform project show`.

norms.quote: is accepted only on standard input. Zero Trust uses the Cloudflare account that
norms.norm: Pass the Access management token only on standard input (`printf ... | void platform zero-trust configure ... --token-stdin --yes`), never as an argument.

norms.quote: `--existing-projects` is required when you enable Zero Trust and
norms.norm: --existing-projects <protected|public> is required when enabling Zero Trust and rejected once enabled; add --existing-projects public when enabling from a disabled configuration; omit --protect-new-projects to make new projects public.

norms.quote: already protected configuration to public-only rules, first disable it
norms.norm: To switch an already protected configuration to public-only rules, first disable it; Access may block traffic during the transition in a Default-Deny account.

norms.quote: `void platform zero-trust reconcile` to resume the saved operation. Protected
norms.norm: If zero-trust status stays configuring or disabling run `void platform zero-trust reconcile`; `status --check` compares with Cloudflare Access.

norms.quote: Void rejects Bypass and Service Auth policies and rules that allow
norms.norm: Select at least one Allow policy matching people by identity; Void rejects Bypass and Service Auth policies and Everyone/service-token rules. The token needs Access: Apps and Policies Write plus Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups Read.
norms.detect: 'Void rejects Bypass and Service Auth policies'.

norms.quote: A project name is not accepted because the Worker name comes from `cloudflare.name` in `void.config.ts`.
norms.norm: On a Cloudflare target `void project status` takes no project name; set the Worker name with cloudflare.name in void.config.ts.

norms.quote: State is stored in `.void/project.json`.
norms.norm: `void project link [name]` links the directory to a hosted project (state in .void/project.json); direct Cloudflare apps use cloudflare.name and need no linking.

norms.quote: Invitations can target only an email address already registered to a user on that platform
norms.norm: Invite only emails already registered on the platform; only the invited account can accept or decline; `void project team` is not available for direct Cloudflare projects; owner alone deletes the project.

norms.quote: Readers can view the project but cannot deploy.
norms.norm: Roles: reader (view), collaborator (deploy and manage deploy prerequisites), admin (also domains, email destinations, GitHub, team); owner alone deletes the project.

norms.quote: the invited application, run `void project link` in an unlinked checkout of
norms.norm: After accepting an invitation, run `void project link` in an unlinked checkout of the invited application; accepting leaves directory links intact.

norms.quote: administrator can run `void project zero-trust reconcile` before you retry.
norms.norm: If deploy or rollback is refused due to a protection change, the owner or a project administrator runs `void project zero-trust reconcile` before retry; `public` does not change the platform default; not for direct Cloudflare.

norms.quote: Manage revocable `aud: deploy` credentials for one Void platform project.
norms.norm: Use `void project token create --name <n> --expires-in <1-90 days>` for CI deploy credentials; they can only call deploy endpoints.

norms.quote: Create and renew display the bearer value once; replace the stored secret
norms.norm: Create/renew show the token once; after `renew` replace the stored CI secret immediately because the previous credential is revoked; project deletion and owner suspension also stop its use; login-method disablement does not revoke it.

norms.quote: Store the printed `VOID_TOKEN` and `VOID_API_URL` in the CI secret manager.
norms.norm: Store the printed VOID_TOKEN and VOID_API_URL in the CI secret manager; on an Access-protected platform with prerendering or remote proxy bindings store VOID_ACCESS_CREDENTIALS as an origin-keyed JSON secret with both exact HTTPS origins (API and proxy), using distinct pairs if the Access policies require it.

norms.quote: Logs include top-level `console.*` calls and uncaught errors captured by Cloudflare Tail.
norms.norm: Errors you catch and save only to your database do not appear in `void project logs`; also log them with console.error() or logger.error() from void/log.
norms.detect: In a catch clause, a console.error/logger.error call is absent (the clause swallows or only stores the error). Escapes: error logged by a called helper.
norms.bad:
// routes/save.ts
try { await save(); } catch (e) { await db.insert(errors).values({ m: String(e) }); }
norms.good:
// routes/save.ts
try { await save(); } catch (e) { console.error('Save failed:', e); throw e; }

norms.quote: Logging only `error.message` shows no stack.
norms.norm: On hosted Void targets pass the Error object itself to console.error (console.error('Save failed:', error)); logging only error.message shows no stack.
norms.detect: A console.error(...)/logger.error(...) call whose only non-literal arguments are `<ident>.message` member expressions of a catch parameter, with no argument being the catch parameter itself.

norms.quote: use `void project requests --status 5xx`.
norms.norm: For errors that never reach your Worker (edge routing, static requests) use `void project requests --status 5xx`; it records no paths; hosted-only; use `void project logs` for per-URL detail.

norms.quote: On a direct Cloudflare target, `--filter` becomes Cloudflare's live search
norms.norm: On direct Cloudflare, `void project logs` is a live tail: --filter is live search, --deployment selects a Worker Version, --level error selects error invocations, --range does not select history.

norms.quote: If the target deployment has fewer applied migrations than the current one, a warning is shown listing the migration diff before confirmation
norms.norm: `void project rollback` warns when the target has fewer applied migrations than the current one; rollback restores code, not database; use `void db restore` for D1.

norms.quote: On Cloudflare, use a complete Worker Version ID or an unambiguous prefix.
norms.norm: On Cloudflare roll back with a complete Worker Version ID or unambiguous prefix; restores triggers only when both versions have complete trigger snapshots; use --platform cloudflare for a one-off Cloudflare deployment.

norms.quote: This command is hosted-only. Direct Cloudflare deploys are local operations
norms.norm: `void project cancel` is hosted-only and cancels only an active deployment; it asks for confirmation.

norms.quote: Permanently delete a hosted Void project and all its resources
norms.norm: `void project delete` permanently deletes a hosted project and all resources (databases, KV, R2, deployments); requires typing the slug; --force skips the prompt; never use --force unasked.

norms.quote: For direct Cloudflare targets this command refuses to run.
norms.norm: `void project delete` refuses on direct Cloudflare targets; verify ownership and remove resources explicitly with Cloudflare tooling.

norms.quote: This command is hosted-only. For direct Cloudflare targets, redeploy or purge the configured ISR KV namespace yourself.
norms.norm: `void project purge-cache` is hosted-only; on direct Cloudflare redeploy or purge the configured ISR KV namespace yourself.

norms.quote: List production secret names for the saved target. Secret values are never printed.
norms.norm: `void secret list` prints names only; direct Cloudflare targets query the Worker named in void.config.ts; --project is hosted-only.

norms.quote: stdin: `echo -n "abcd" | void secret put API_KEY`
norms.norm: Set production secrets with `void secret put NAME` (masked prompt or stdin); avoid inline NAME=value where shell history is recorded.
norms.good: void secret put API_KEY (masked) or stdin

norms.quote: On a direct Cloudflare target, the value is stored as an encrypted Worker secret.
norms.norm: On direct Cloudflare targets `void secret put` stores an encrypted Worker secret; use it rather than plaintext vars.

norms.quote: Upload production server values from a dotenv file stored outside your project.
norms.norm: For `void secret sync <file>` use a dotenv file stored outside the project containing only production server keys declared in env.ts; leave out local development credentials and public VITE_* values.
norms.detect: File outside repo and env.ts content.

norms.quote: Existing remote secrets absent from the file are kept.
norms.norm: `void secret sync` does not remove other remote secrets; every entry must be a server key declared in env.ts with a value that passes validation; --yes skips confirmation.

norms.quote: Direct Cloudflare targets reject `--project`
norms.norm: Direct Cloudflare targets reject --project for secret commands and use the pinned root Cloudflare config; hosted project resolution is --project, env var, linked project.

norms.quote: secret writes and deletes return a retryable conflict while a deployment or rollback is in progress
norms.norm: On hosted projects wait for a deployment or rollback to finish and retry a secret write or delete that returns a conflict; the stored secret is unchanged.

norms.quote: Exits non-zero if a required key is missing or a readable value is invalid.
norms.norm: Run `void env check` (local) or `void env check --remote` (build-shell client values and remote secret names) to validate env.ts; it exits non-zero on a missing required key or invalid value.
norms.detect: 'Exits non-zero if a required key is missing'.

norms.quote: use this command after a fresh clone or to refresh stale types in non-dev contexts.
norms.norm: Run `void env types` to regenerate .void/env.d.ts from env.ts after a fresh clone or in non-dev contexts; never edit .void/env.d.ts by hand.

norms.quote: refuses to upload if any required key is missing
norms.norm: `void deploy` validates env.ts with remote secrets and refuses to upload when a required key is missing; no separate `env check` is needed.
norms.detect: 'refuses to upload if any required key is missing'.

norms.quote: Before moving a deployed definition, copy the suggested `name` into
norms.norm: Before moving a deployed Durable State/Room/WebSocket definition file, copy the name from `void info` into defineDurableState(), defineRoom() or defineWebSocket() and keep it after the move.
norms.detect: In a file that calls defineDurableState/defineRoom/defineWebSocket, flag a call with no explicit `name` option; it cannot know which are deployed or moved. Escapes: names passed through variables.
norms.good:
// durable/counter.ts
export default defineDurableState({ name: 'counter', initial: 0 });

norms.quote: Adopt a suggested name only after identifying the resource you moved.
norms.norm: Adopt a suggested name from `void info` only after identifying the moved resource; resources recorded in void.lock.json without a matching definition are listed separately; if no name is suggested restore the original source and inspect.
norms.detect: Judgement across lock file and code.

norms.quote: It runs locally without authentication, network requests, or file generation.
norms.norm: `void info [--json]` is safe and local; use it to inspect inferred Durable State and WebSocket resource names (source file, name, class, binding).

norms.quote: `void migrate` converts legacy `void.json` and root `wrangler.jsonc` or `wrangler.json` files into `void.config.ts`.
norms.norm: Convert legacy void.json and root wrangler.jsonc/json into void.config.ts with `void migrate` (backups in .void/config-migration/, IDs in void.lock.json); `void init` and `void deploy` migrate automatically; resolve conflicting Cloudflare configs first and keep the void package and CLI on one version.

norms.quote: The command adds generated `.cloudflare/` and `.void-wrangler.jsonc` files to `.gitignore` as needed.
norms.norm: Keep generated .cloudflare/ and .void-wrangler.jsonc in .gitignore; review and commit void.config.ts, void.lock.json and .gitignore after `void migrate`.

norms.quote: The new app's `void.config.ts` turns on
norms.norm: A new `void init` app's void.config.ts turns on routing.typedRoutes.
norms.detect: In void.config.ts, the config object lacks routing: { typedRoutes: true }. Escapes: config built from variables or spreads.
norms.good:
// void.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ routing: { typedRoutes: true } });

norms.quote: For non-interactive scaffolding, choose `--deploy none` and run `void connect` later to sign in.
norms.norm: For scripted or agent scaffolding pass flags: void init --toolchain vite-plus|vite --framework react|vue|svelte|solid --starter sqlite|postgresql|mysql|static --deploy none (then `void connect` later).

norms.quote: Vite+ projects install dependencies through `vp install`
norms.norm: Vite+ projects install dependencies with `vp install`; Void preserves existing package-manager versions and lockfiles.

norms.quote: In an existing app, Void adds missing dependencies and scripts and updates the Vite config.
norms.norm: In an existing app `void init` edits dependencies, scripts and the Vite config; if it cannot edit the config it prints a snippet to add; review the diff.

norms.quote: Existing projects prompt before the file
norms.norm: `void init` creates a minimal AGENTS.md pointing to node_modules/void/docs/ and links skills for detected agents; existing projects prompt before the file is created or appended; CI/non-interactive runs leave existing instructions unchanged.

norms.quote: Use `--git` to initialize without a prompt or `--no-git` to skip it.
norms.norm: Use --git or --no-git with `void init`; CI requires --git to initialize; workspace packages do not accept these flags.

norms.quote: These flags can be combined and skip the other wizard steps.
norms.norm: `void init --tsconfig` updates TypeScript config and `void init --github` creates the GitHub Actions deployment workflow; combined they skip other wizard steps (agent setup still runs).

norms.quote: For Cloudflare workflows, add a `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` repository secret.
norms.norm: For the generated Cloudflare GitHub workflow add a CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN repository secret (and DATABASE_URL for PostgreSQL/MySQL apps).

norms.quote: Authorize the repository with `void github connect <project> --repo <owner/repo> --executor github_actions`.
norms.norm: For Void platforms with GitHub Actions support authorize the repository with `void github connect <project> --repo <owner/repo> --executor github_actions` (short-lived OIDC credentials); core self-hosted platforms do not support it.

norms.quote: Run it after a fresh clone or before typechecking in CI.
norms.norm: Run `void prepare` after a fresh clone and before typechecking in CI; it generates .void/ types and TypeScript configuration without starting dev or building; never hand-edit .void/ and keep it ignored.
norms.bad: tsc in CI with no prepare
